event.summary: Restart failure deletes a private tmux server's socket before its explicit guard runs
event.detail: Reviewed commits: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513 (generic harness guard removal) and dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 (assigned main.rs registration enabling old_terminals fixtures). TLDR: a failing old-terminal cleanup test can leave its private tmux server running after deleting the directory needed to stop it, so neither the explicit guard nor the later dead-run sweep can reach it. This revises the original c3 no-unguarded-server conclusion: the guard exists, but does not own the directory across failure. Source: old_terminals.rs:266,400,536 constructs OldServer beside h, with a TmuxServerGuard storing only its socket path; tests at 333-335,449-451,569-571 move h into restart_supervisor while OldServer remains in the caller. harness.rs:1133-1146 destructures self and holds TestDir state inside the restart future, then awaits retire_supervisor before returning a new Harness. retire_supervisor:1100-1106 explicitly panics when old connection tasks fail to drain in ten seconds, before the new supervisor can end tmux. Unwinding that future drops state first, while the outer OldServer guard is still live; TestDir::drop ends terminal hosts only and removes the state directory. Later the outer guard has no reachable socket for its shutdown. Successful restart does not expose the ordering failure because startup ends the server normally. The no-server fixture already kills its server before restart, so its restart is not a live-server leak route; the scoped-agent and mixed-tab tests do retain live servers. Suggested bucket: other (maintainer test resource cleanup; no established catastrophic impact). Confidence: likely from source; exact final guard refusal after parent deletion is being checked next, no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; forbidden coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: no shipped security/work-loss route or catastrophic tooling route established. Caveat: requires a test failure during consumed-harness restart before startup kills the server, such as the explicit retire timeout, not a successful test. Fix direction: retain the directory in an owner that drops after the explicit server guard across the restart future as well as caller unwinding, or move explicit server ownership into the consumed fixture so teardown order survives failure. Remaining readily checkable premise: verify the guard has no retained peer handle independent of the removed socket; inspected public struct stores socket/executable only, and final shutdown implementation is next.

event.summary: Restart failure deletes the tmux socket before the explicit server guard runs
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4, with the preceding assigned harness ownership change at 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: if an old-terminal test fails while restarting its supervisor, it can leave a private tmux server running after deleting the directory required to stop it. This overturns c3's original proposed drop: explicit guard presence is insufficient when directory ownership moves into an inner future. Details: main.rs:111 enables old_terminals. old_terminals.rs:266 and536 construct OldServer after the original Harness; its fields at27-30 hold paths and TmuxServerGuard, not the TestDir. At332-334 and572-574 the live-server tests consume h through restart_supervisor while the server guard stays in the caller. harness.rs:1130-1136 moves TestDir into that restart future and awaits retire_supervisor; the latter has an explicit ten-second assertion at1100-1104 before the new supervisor is built. If that assertion fails, unwinding drops the inner future's TestDir before the outer OldServer guard. TestDir::drop at farhelm-teststate/src/lib.rs:794-805 stops only terminal hosts, and removes the directory when those stops succeed. TmuxServerGuard stores only socket/executable (tmux/guard.rs:24-27), so its eventual Drop at75-96 acquires shutdown authority afresh from the now-deleted path. shutdown_tmux_server at tmux.rs:242-244 returns refused when validate_socket cannot read the missing parent (368-369); refused at290-297 performs no protocol attempt and has no fallback. This is documentation correctness, not a failing flood test or a claim of current terminal-history loss. Actual source agrees: terminal-host/src/host.rs:455-487 reaps the child, drains available output and journals the exit without setting host shutdown; the event loop at347 continues processing its client.
